content.intro: This lesson introduces asynchronous tasks, queues, and synchronization as part of concurrency, parallelism, and asynchronous programming. It turns the curriculum heading into a short, practical concept guide with a visual, example, and checks to try locally.
content.why_it_matters: Choose concurrency from the workload and coordination needs. Cancellation, timeouts, shared-state safety, and graceful error handling matter as much as speed.

content_blocks.code:
import asyncio

async def main():
    await asyncio.sleep(0)
    print("Task completed")

asyncio.run(main())
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run with python main.py. Async is useful for concurrent I/O; it does not automatically make CPU-bound work faster.
